title: Elimination Game
statement:
Write down the integers `1, 2, ..., n` in increasing order. Then remove numbers in rounds, switching direction each round, until exactly one number is left:

- Rounds 1, 3, 5, ... sweep from the left end to the right end: the first number still on the list is removed, the next is kept, the next is removed, and so on, alternating to the end.
- Rounds 2, 4, 6, ... do the same sweep from the right end to the left end, so the last number still on the list is removed first.

Given the integer `n`, return the one number that survives.
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating the rounds with a real list costs O(n) memory and time, far too much for `n = 10^9`. But after every round the survivors are still evenly spaced: they form an arithmetic sequence. Such a sequence is described by its first number, the gap between neighbours and how many numbers it has, so it is enough to track those three values. Each round halves the count and doubles the gap; the only question is whether the first number is removed.

## Approach

1. Start with `head = 1`, `step = 1`, `remaining = n` and `fromLeft = true`.
2. While more than one number remains, decide whether the current `head` is removed in this round:
   - a left-to-right sweep always removes the first number;
   - a right-to-left sweep removes it only when `remaining` is odd, because then the alternation starting from the right end lands on it.
3. If it is removed, the new first number is the next one along: `head += step`.
4. Every other number disappears, so `remaining` halves (rounding down) and `step` doubles. Flip `fromLeft`.
5. When one number remains, it is `head`.

## Example 1, step by step

For `n = 9`: `head = 1`, `step = 1`, `remaining = 9`.

- Round 1 goes from the left, so `head` becomes 2; now `remaining = 4`, `step = 2` (the list is 2, 4, 6, 8).
- Round 2 goes from the right with an even count, so 2 survives and `head` stays 2; `remaining = 2`, `step = 4` (2, 6).
- Round 3 goes from the left, so `head` becomes 6; `remaining = 1`. The answer is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n): `remaining` halves every round.
- Space: O(1): only four numbers are tracked.

## Pitfalls

- A right-to-left round with an even count keeps the first number; forgetting the parity test gives 4 instead of 2 for `n = 4`.
- Halve `remaining` with floor division; in JavaScript `remaining / 2` alone produces fractions.
- Double `step` after using it, not before, or `head` jumps too far.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `head` | the smallest number still on the list |
| `step` | the gap between neighbouring survivors |
| `remaining` | how many numbers are still on the list |
| `fromLeft` | whether the current round sweeps left to right |

narration.2: Before any round, the smallest number on the list is 1.
narration.4: All n numbers are still on the list.
narration.5: The first round sweeps from the left.
narration.7: Keep playing rounds until a single number is left.
narration.8: The smallest number is removed on every left sweep, and on a right sweep only when the count is odd.
narration.9: If it is removed, the next survivor along becomes the new smallest number.
narration.11: Every other number is removed, so the count halves, rounding down.
narration.12: The survivors are now twice as far apart.
narration.13: The next round sweeps the other way.
narration.15: Only one number remains, and it is the tracked head.
